### 1 — Scene
A cooked meal with long-stem broccoli, a browned meat patty or cutlet, rice, a pale yellow portion that appears to be scrambled egg, and red tomato-based sauce. Strong sunlight makes the rice and egg identification uncertain.

### 2 — Vessel
A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** in diameter.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight and energy
Areas below partition the food-covered surface rather than counting overlapping foods twice. Heights are estimated average pile depths.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked rice | 25% | 133 × 1.8 = 239 ml | 0.8 | 191 g | 130 | 248 kcal |
| Cooked long-stem broccoli | 23% | 122 × 1.8 = 220 ml | 0.5 | 110 g | 35 | 39 kcal |
| Browned meat patty/cutlet | 10% | 53 × 1.5 = 80 ml | 1.0 | 80 g | 240 | 192 kcal |
| Scrambled egg, apparent | 12% | 64 × 1.5 = 96 ml | 0.9 | 86 g | 160 | 138 kcal |
| Tomato-based sauce with pieces | 5% | 27 × 0.7 = 19 ml | 1.0 | 19 g | 60 | 11 kcal |

No separate oil quantity is clearly distinguishable, so none is added.

### 8 — Sanity check
The areas total **75% of the plate**, consistent with the visible uncovered rim and gaps. The estimate is **486 g and 628 kcal**, plausible for the substantial food coverage. The largest uncertainty is the identity of the brightly lit pale foods.
